groups.name: N0n
groups.profile: First seen by researchers mid-September 2026; debuted threatening to destroy backups/shadow copies alongside the usual double extortion; initial access reportedly via infostealer credentials. Widely reported as US/financial-services-heavy, though today's claims skew manufacturing & professional services.
groups.sectors: Energy & Utilities, Manufacturing, Professional Services, Technology

groups.name: qilin
groups.profile: One of 2026's most active RaaS brands (aka Agenda), active since 2022; affiliate payouts reportedly 70–85%; added DDoS pressure tactics in 2025; broad global footprint across manufacturing, construction, professional services, tech and retail.
groups.sectors: Manufacturing, Professional Services, Retail & E-Commerce, Technology

groups.name: emperador
groups.profile: New RaaS first observed August 2026, initially focused on APAC municipal/government targets; claims ChaCha20 double extortion negotiated over Tox/Session with up to 90% affiliate split. Today's claims widen into tech and food & beverage.
groups.sectors: Agriculture and Food Production, Government & Defense, Technology

groups.name: Falcon
groups.profile: Young RaaS; Tor leak site first posted early August 2026, with claims of hundreds of GB to multi-TB stolen per victim. First appearance of this group in Breach Wire.

groups.name: Whitearmor
groups.profile: Leak-site handle with limited independent public profiling available. Also posted a non-victim social-media callout this issue (see footer) rather than a named-victim claim.

groups.name: anubis
groups.profile: RaaS notable for an integrated wiper mode (/WIPEMODE) layered on top of double extortion; first seen late 2024 as a rebrand of Sphinx; prior reported targets include healthcare, construction and engineering in the US, Canada, Australia and Peru.

groups.name: HYFLOCK
groups.profile: RaaS launched May 2026; operators claim LockBit/Qilin lineage; vendors disagree on cipher (HC-128 vs AES-128-CTR+RSA-4096); double extortion with a free-leak option, negotiated over qTox/Tor.

groups.name: majinahanashi
groups.profile: Surfaced June 2026; claims AES-256 per-file encryption with a .majin extension and a README.txt note; prior reported targets span retail, food service and healthcare across multiple countries.

groups.name: Panzer
groups.profile: Mid-tier RaaS active since mid-2026 with a reported ~20 victims per 60 days; third-party trackers describe Europe/Middle East/Africa-leaning targeting and limited public profiling.

groups.name: securotrop
groups.profile: Trackers describe it as having evolved from, or operated within, the Qilin affiliate network before going independent. Sources disagree on current activity — one tracker lists it inactive since February 2026 — but it posted a fresh claim in this window.
